Meaning: still the ethical kind of double bind, defined as offering the person asked two options that are both genuinely safe. "An ethical one" becomes the full term ("one" meant the double bind), and "offers two ... routes" becomes "gives someone a choice between two ... things to do"; "a choice" and "someone" are what offering two options to a person already meant, and the example under it (allow a feeling of warmth, or a feeling of space) fits "things to do". It reads more definitional and a little heavier than his one-line version, in the register of the paragraph above, and the full term now opens two sentences in a row (this one and the unchanged "Ethical Double Bind Questions might be:").
